documents.name: Context Graph Docs — README
documents.title: Context Graph Docs
documents.summary: Entry point for the Context Graph doc set: what project memory is, the shipped v1.5 surface, and the OSS default install path.
documents.description: The index page of Potpie's Context Graph documentation, carrying the status header 'reflects code on main @ 8dd175bc, last reviewed 2026-06-29'. It frames the Context Graph as durable, shared project memory for AI agents — a compact store of sourced claims (decisions, ownership, infra topology, prior bugs/fixes, conventions, features) so an agent does not rebuild context from raw code, PRs, tickets and chat on every task. It states the shipped contract versions (data plane GRAPH_CONTRACT_VERSION v1.5, ONTOLOGY_VERSION 2026-06-graph), the target OSS default flow (`pip install potpie` then `potpie setup`), and that the OSS/CLI default graph backend is the embedded `falkordb_lite` with no Docker, Neo4j or cloud key required. It also flags the roadmap items that are NOT wired: managed-backend routing (`pot use --managed`, the `cloud` group) raises CapabilityNotImplemented, and the external Event Ledger clients are TODO stubs.

documents.name: Context Graph Vision
documents.title: Context Graph Vision
documents.summary: Why the Context Graph exists: claims-not-payloads, one CLI for humans and agents, and the storage-is-an-adapter principle.
documents.description: The 'why' document for Potpie project memory. It names the problem — decisions scattered across PRs, ADRs, Slack threads and tickets; ownership and topology living in tribal memory; prior bugs unretrievable by symptom; agents starting every task with no durable memory. Its central design rule is 'claims, not payloads': the graph stores compact sourced, time-stamped claims plus source refs and deliberately never holds PR diffs, document bodies, chat transcripts, logs, webhook archives or telemetry, with semantic indexes and analytics rollups treated as rebuildable projections over the canonical claim store ('the graph model is the invariant, physical storage is an adapter'). It also establishes that there is no separate human-vs-agent API: both drive the same `potpie` CLI, while agents may additionally use exactly four in-process MCP tools (context_resolve, context_search, context_record, context_status).

documents.name: Context Graph Architecture
documents.title: Context Graph Architecture
documents.summary: The implementation map: hexagonal layers, the two composition roots, the daemon, and the swappable GraphBackend.
documents.description: The engineering map of the context-engine. It documents the ports-and-adapters layering — `domain/` (three ontology catalogs, contract constants, ports, DTOs, ranking, coherence, identity, no I/O), `application/` (graph_service, graph_workbench, agent_context, read_orchestrator, envelope_builder, nudge_service, skill_manager, semantic mutation validator/lowering, reconciliation_validation, the 9 readers), `adapters/inbound|outbound`, `bootstrap/`, and `host/`. Its most load-bearing section is the two-composition-roots split: `host_wiring.py` (the local agent spine, default backend falkordb_lite) versus `bootstrap/ingestion_server.py` (the HTTP ingestion server, default backend neo4j) — conflating them is called out as the most common architectural mistake. It also corrects the 'future Graph V2' framing: the `potpie graph …` workbench ships today as V1.5 and the string `v2` survives only as GRAPH_WORKBENCH_CONTRACT_VERSION, the transport envelope version.

documents.name: Ontology & Graph Contract
documents.title: Ontology & Graph Contract
documents.summary: Canonical reference for the 24 entity labels, 25 public predicates + RELATED_TO, 7 truth classes and the evidence-gating rules.
documents.description: The vocabulary spec that `potpie graph catalog`, `describe` and `status` return, enumerated from `domain/ontology.py` rather than aspirational prose (it explicitly replaces the older workbench-ontology.md). It defines the 24 entity labels, the 25 public predicates plus the RELATED_TO soft-fail fallback, the identity/key-prefix rules, the singleton registry (OWNED_BY is the only singleton predicate), and the evidence model: TRUTH_TO_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH mapping authoritative_fact/source_observation to `deterministic`, user_decision/preference/timeline_event to `attested`, agent_claim to `stated`, quality_finding to `inferred`, with EVIDENCE_REQUIRED_TRUTH_CLASSES = {authoritative_fact, source_observation}. It carries an explicit caveat that two evidence-strength vocabularies exist in code — `ontology.EVIDENCE_STRENGTHS` (deterministic/attested/inferred/hypothesized) versus the ranker's `_STRENGTH_TO_SCORE` (deterministic/attested/stated/inferred/speculative) — and that only the ranker vocabulary is consumed.

documents.name: Querying / Reading the Context Graph
documents.title: Querying / Reading the Context Graph
documents.summary: The read side: two altitudes over one data plane, the single read trunk, ranking, coverage, and the anti-phantom-vocabulary rule.
documents.description: Owns how an agent or human pulls ranked, sourced evidence out of project memory. Its governing principle, repeated on every read path, is 'Potpie returns ranked evidence, never a synthesized answer' — there is no server-side answer summary anywhere in the read trunk. It documents the two read altitudes over the same claim store (the 4-tool MCP agent contract bound by AgentContextService, and the CLI-only Graph Surface Lite workbench: catalog/read/search-entities/neighborhood/describe/status/history), the single P8/P9 read trunk through ReadOrchestrator.resolve → 9 readers → ClaimQueryPort.find_claims → RankingService → EnvelopeBuilder → AgentEnvelope, the six-factor weighted ranker, per-include CoverageReport statuses (complete/partial/sparse/empty), and the anti-phantom-vocabulary rule that returns `unknown_include` instead of a silent zero when an include is not in the vocabulary.

documents.name: Writing the Context Graph
documents.title: Writing the Context Graph
documents.summary: The write path: tiered stack, flat semantic DSL, propose → commit --verify, the single write door, soft-fail downgrade, inbox and quality.
documents.description: How facts get into the graph. It establishes that the canonical write door is `graph propose` → `graph commit --verify` and that `graph mutate` is a legacy wrapper, with the immediate-apply path (DefaultGraphService.mutate) now reachable only via `record`/`context_record`. It walks the tiers: semantic DSL (domain/semantic_mutations.py), validation + per-op MutationRisk, lowering to a MutationBatch, the two spines, the pre-apply gate, and `apply_mutation_batch` in adapters/outbound/graph/apply_plan.py writing the Position-B canonical store `(:Entity)-[:RELATES_TO]->(:Entity)`. Section 8 is the soft-fail downgrade contract that this fixture's QualityIssue markers come from: with CONTEXT_ENGINE_ONTOLOGY_SOFT_FAIL=1 the validator drops unknown labels, falls ADR → Document/Observation, coerces invalid lifecycle to `unknown`, rewrites unknown edge types → RELATED_TO at confidence 0.3, drops endpoint-mismatched edges, and may attach a QualityIssue node per downgrade.

documents.name: Potpie CLI Flow & Command Reference
documents.title: Potpie CLI Flow & Command Reference
documents.summary: The full grouped `potpie` command surface with flags, shared plumbing, and the canonical user journey.
documents.description: The one doc allowed to restate flags in full: the complete `potpie` CLI reference, pinned at 'reflects code on main @ 49e12528, last reviewed 2026-07-02' — the freshest header in the doc set. It describes `potpie/cli/main.py build_app()` as the single console entrypoint (one Typer root with three global options: --json, --verbose/-v, --version) and the invariant routing `CLI → HostShell → service(s) → ports`. It documents the shared plumbing in `commands/_common.py` — `get_host()` returning a daemon-backed RemoteHostShell by default, `contract()`, and `resolve_pot_id` — plus every command group: doctor, login, setup, pot, source, search/resolve/record wrappers, skills, daemon, ledger, and the whole `graph …` workbench. Use this doc to answer 'what flag does X', 'why does the CLI need a daemon', or 'which command am I supposed to run'.

documents.name: The Agent Mutation Flow (design target)
documents.title: The Agent Mutation Flow
documents.summary: Aspirational seven-stage agent write loop (orient → extract → resolve → author → check → commit+verify → reconcile); explicitly not current state.
documents.description: A design-target doc drafted 2026-07-09 that describes the ideal loop for an agent writing to the graph, with tools marked ✅ (shipped) or 🔧 (proposed, mapping to the repair roadmap `.tmp/context-graph-repair-roadmap-2026-07-08.md`). Its thesis is that agents are good at understanding work and bad at byte-perfect bookkeeping — minting the exact key an earlier agent minted, spelling `prod` the same way twice — so every hand-off should be a typed artifact (a JSON file with a contract) rather than prose discipline in a skill, because 'prose discipline demonstrably did not survive contact with real agents (2026-07-02 e2e)'. It defines seven stages (ORIENT, EXTRACT, RESOLVE, AUTHOR, CHECK, COMMIT+VERIFY, RECONCILE) and two sizes of the same loop: micro (in-session, skip orient/extract) and macro (full ingestion with a candidate manifest as backbone). The header warns loudly: do not treat this as current-state reference — writing.md owns the shipped path.

documents.name: Ingestion, the Event Ledger(s) & the Nudge Trigger Model
documents.title: Ingestion, the Event Ledger(s) & the Nudge Trigger Model
documents.summary: How source events enter the graph and how zero-token nudges push the right slice back to an in-session agent; disambiguates the two 'ledgers'.
documents.description: Covers the ingestion side and the nudge model, opening with a correction because both subsystems drifted hard from their original designs. Point one: there are two completely different 'ledgers' — the REAL internal Postgres event store (adapters/outbound/postgres/{reconciliation_ledger,ingestion_event_store,batch_repository,ledger}.py) whose lifecycle vocabulary is `queued / processing / done / error` and which has no cursor concept, versus the external Event Ledger product seam (domain/ports/ledger/*, adapters/outbound/ledger/{managed,self_hosted}_client.py) which is mostly TODO stubs and owns the per-(pot, source) cursor. The old six-state vocabulary (pending/processing/applied/failed_retryable/failed_terminal/timed_out) described the external consumer that does not exist yet. Point two: scanners and most connectors are gone — repo/PR/ticket ingestion is now harness-led via skills or a server-side event flow. Section 7 documents the zero-token nudge policy (domain/nudge.py), NudgeService, the ~/.potpie/nudge_sessions.json dedup ledger bounded to 500 sessions, and the Claude plugin hook `potpie_nudge.py`; a nudge never ingests, it only reads or instructs.

documents.name: Context Engine Observability
documents.title: Observability
documents.summary: The backend-neutral ObservabilityPort, the NoOp default, and why local OSS is dark unless an operator opts in.
documents.description: Documents observability as a thin domain seam: `domain/ports/observability.py ObservabilityPort`, which the domain and application layers emit spans and metrics through. Core code never imports `opentelemetry` directly — that import exists only inside `adapters/outbound/observability/otel.py`, which is what keeps the backend swappable (OTLP → Tempo/Prometheus today). The default sink is NoOpObservability so every call site is safe to invoke unconditionally and a local CLI/daemon stays completely dark unless explicitly configured via CONTEXT_ENGINE_OBSERVABILITY=console|<truthy for OTLP>; observability never raises into a caller and can never fail a request. Both composition roots (potpie/services/host_wiring.py and bootstrap/ingestion_server.py) wire the same port. Search this doc for 'no traces locally', 'spans missing', 'why is telemetry off by default'.

documents.name: Skills & Harness-Led Intelligence
documents.title: Skills & Harness-Led Intelligence
documents.summary: Why the reasoning lives in the user's harness, the 8-skill bundle, DefaultSkillManager install targets, and the separate server-side reconciliation surface.
documents.description: States Potpie's central anti-goal concretely: no Potpie-owned LLM or reconciliation agent as the canonical source of graph intelligence. The reasoning that turns a repo, PR, ticket or bug into durable memory lives in the user's coding harness (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, OpenCode) on the user's own model subscription; Potpie validates, lowers, commits, audits and ranks. A skill is pure instruction text — a SKILL.md with no executable code and no new tools. It documents the bundle catalog (`potpie/services/skills/bundle_catalog.py` parsing YAML front-matter into SkillInfo), that there are 8 skills in the agent bundle and 7 in the Claude Code plugin (everything except potpie-cli), and the per-harness install targets: ~/.claude/skills, ~/.agents/skills, ~/.cursor/skills, ~/.config/opencode/skills. It closes by insisting the two skill surfaces are never conflated: user-installed bundle skills versus the off-by-default server-side reconciliation skills loaded by pydantic_deep_agent.py with a different tool surface.

documents.name: Context Graph Benchmarks (plan)
documents.title: Context Graph Benchmarks
documents.summary: Design intent for the graph-quality benchmark that runs the same scenarios across every GraphBackend to produce comparable score deltas.
documents.description: A planning/reference artifact, explicitly not a per-run log — the harness itself lives at `potpie/context-engine/benchmarks/` (cli.py entrypoint, core/, evaluators/, use_cases/, fixtures/). The benchmark validates graph quality rather than OSS packaging or latency, running identical scenarios against every real backend behind the GraphBackend contract (in_memory, embedded, falkordb_lite, falkordb, neo4j) so an ontology, reader or storage change produces a comparable score delta. Reads go through the shipped V1.5 workbench (`graph read` over named views); writes go through propose → commit --verify. It notes the managed backend profile and external Event Ledger replay are bench targets but not functional, and that the legacy ContextGraphQuery/ContextGraphStrategy model in `domain/graph_query.py` is vestigial and now survives only as bench plumbing.

documents.name: Sandbox Core Setup
documents.title: Sandbox Core Setup
documents.summary: The RepoCache / Workspace / Runtime model behind the hexagonal sandbox module agents use to clone, edit and run user repos.
documents.description: Design doc for the isolated place Potpie agents inspect and change user repositories: clone once, reuse the repo later, create worktrees for new work, run commands, edit files, run tests, and resume the same state in a later session. Its key move is refusing to treat 'sandbox' as one thing — a RepoCache is the durable git mirror that avoids recloning, a Workspace is the durable working tree or worktree the agent sees, and a Runtime is the compute environment that runs commands against a workspace and may be stopped, recreated or moved without deleting the workspace. The hexagonal module lives at `app/src/sandbox/sandbox/` (domain ports, application service, API client, outbound adapters); local mode wires LocalGitWorkspaceProvider + LocalRepoCacheProvider directly. Goals include letting local container, Docker, Daytona, E2B or future providers run against the same workspace abstraction and supporting explicit eviction policies; non-goals include building a human dev environment like VS Code Remote or Coder.

documents.name: Sandbox Integration Plan
documents.title: Sandbox Integration Plan
documents.summary: Plan to make app/src/sandbox the single repo-materialization library and retire repo_manager + code_changes_manager.
documents.description: The follow-on to sandbox-core-setup: how to turn `app/src/sandbox` into the one library everything in potpie uses to materialize repos and run code, and retire the parallel `app/modules/repo_manager` + `app/modules/intelligence/tools/code_changes_manager` stack. It inventories what already works (domain models, WorkspaceProvider/RuntimeProvider/SandboxStore/LockManager ports, local-git and local-subprocess and docker and daytona adapters, an idempotent per-workspace-locked SandboxService with get_or_create_workspace / get_or_create_runtime / exec / hibernate_runtime / destroy_runtime, E2E tests across all three runtime backends) against what still drives the old path — bare repo + worktree management under `.repos/<owner>/<repo>/` with its own auth chain and eviction, a Redis-backed per-conversation file-edit staging area wrapped in ~20 LangChain StructuredTools, and parsing calling RepoManager.prepare_for_parsing(). It deliberately names tradeoffs rather than deciding them: it is a plan, not a spec.

documents.name: Async Migration Plan — Native Libraries, Step by Step
documents.title: Async Migration Plan
documents.summary: Reverts the asyncio.to_thread wrappers and replaces blocking libraries with native async equivalents, measuring every step.
documents.description: A remediation plan written after code review flagged the previous PRs that wrapped blocking calls in `asyncio.to_thread`: thread-safety bugs from DB sessions passed to worker threads, an unbounded queue in a custom stream generator, daemon-thread-per-stream with no cap, thread pool saturation risk under load, and the observation that a StreamingResponse with a sync generator already runs in Starlette's thread pool so the custom thread+queue was pure overhead. Step 0 is a file-by-file revert table across conversation_routing.py, conversations_router.py, conversation_service.py, redis_streaming.py, api/router.py, tunnel_router.py, tunnel_service.py, socket_service.py, main.py and github_service.py, with an explicit keep-list: `wait_for_task_start(require_running=True)` is a correctness fix, timeouts on requests calls are a safety fix, and `parsing_controller._query_parsing_status_sync` stays an acceptable to_thread bridge until the async DB migration. Search this for 'thread pool saturation', 'to_thread revert', 'redis stream generator async'.

documents.name: VS Code Extension Debug/DAP Handoff
documents.title: VS Code Extension Debug/DAP Handoff
documents.summary: Handoff note (2026-05-25) for two C/C++ debugging failures over the Socket.IO tunnel: RPC timeouts with no tool_response, and missing lldb adapters.
documents.description: A dated engineering handoff describing why C/C++ debugging degrades in the VS Code extension even though the debug agent can reach the local workspace over the Socket.IO tunnel. Failure one: terminal commands such as `gcc -g ...` and `mkdir ...` complete locally while the backend waits until the RPC timeout because no matching `tool_response` arrives on Redis pub/sub — explicitly not believed to be a network or WebSocket reliability problem. Failure two: `get_workspace_debug_context` reports `debug_adapters: ["python", "node"]` on a macOS machine where LLDB and lldb-dap are installed, blocking C/C++ session setup. It records an isolated harness verification after the extension-side terminal fix (`/api/terminal/execute` for `cc -g -o add_numbers add_numbers.c` returning in ~400ms with success=true and exit_code=0; `/api/workspace/debug-context` returning ["python","node","lldb","lldb-dap"]; start-session and set-breakpoints succeeding) and one still-failing path: `/api/debug/snapshot` after continue returns 'Cannot take snapshot: session is running, expected paused'. It states plainly that the run was a smoke test, not a full DAP tool matrix — step-over, step-into, step-out, evaluate, list-sessions and clean stop-session were not covered.

documents.name: Context-Engine CLI Sentry Telemetry
documents.title: Context-Engine CLI Sentry Telemetry
documents.summary: How Sentry is scoped to unexpected CLI failures only, its env-var precedence, and the PII scrubbing guarantees.
documents.description: Documents the CLI-owned Sentry integration under `potpie/context-engine`, deliberately independent of the context-engine telemetry path and legacy/deploy/observability, and used only for unexpected Potpie CLI failures. It specifies environment precedence — process environment, then `.env` values only when POTPIE_ENVIRONMENT resolves to `dev` and only for missing keys, then distribution defaults packaged into the wheel, then code defaults — and notes that `.env` can never set or change POTPIE_ENVIRONMENT. Canonical configuration keys are POTPIE_ENVIRONMENT, POTPIE_SENTRY_DSN (presence enables Sentry), POTPIE_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 (kills all outbound telemetry), POTPIE_SENTRY_ENABLED=0 (Sentry only), POTPIE_SENTRY_RELEASE and POTPIE_SENTRY_DIST; generic SENTRY_* aliases are explicitly not read. Privacy posture is spelled out: send_default_pii=False, include_local_variables=False, max_request_body_size='never', plus before_send event scrubbing and before_breadcrumb breadcrumb scrubbing.

documents.name: Potpie Docs — Introduction
documents.title: Introduction
documents.summary: Public docs landing page: what Potpie is and how the code knowledge graph powers codebase agents.
documents.description: The landing page of the public Mintlify documentation at docs.potpie.ai. It pitches Potpie as a way to build AI agents for your codebase in minutes, and explains the product-facing framing of the code knowledge graph: Potpie breaks a codebase into its constituting parts, builds a knowledge graph of the code's components, and generates inferences at every level so agents can comprehensively answer questions about the codebase. This is the hosted-product framing (repositories, parsing, agents, chat) rather than the CLI/context-graph project-memory framing that lives in the potpie repo's docs/context-graph set — the two vocabularies coexist and readers often confuse them.

documents.name: Potpie Docs — Quickstart
documents.title: Quickstart
documents.summary: One-click onboarding: install the Potpie GitHub app, select repo + branch, create your first codebase agent.
documents.description: The getting-started walkthrough for the hosted product. It instructs the user to install the Potpie GitHub app (github.com/apps/potpie-ai) at signup so they can select which repositories to create codebase agents for, then land on the dashboard. It walks through selecting a repository and branch from the new-chat screen so the conversation carries the correct codebase context, and then creating and talking to a first agent. Search this for 'how do I connect my repo', 'select branch for chat', 'GitHub app install', 'first agent'.

documents.name: Potpie Docs — Local / Self-Hosted Setup
documents.title: Local Setup
documents.summary: Step-by-step self-hosting: Firebase service account, Portkey observability key, GitHub app for login, and the local API server on :8001.
documents.description: The self-hosting runbook for standing up the Potpie server locally. It covers creating a Firebase project and generating a service account key renamed to `firebase_service_account.json` at the source root for auth, signing up for Portkey and setting PORTKEY_API_KEY for LLM observability and monitoring, and creating a GitHub app (e.g. `potpie-auth`) to enable GitHub login. The companion getting-started page assumes the API server is reachable at http://localhost:8001 and walks the raw curl flow — POST /api/v1/login for a bearer token, then submitting a parsing request for a repo and branch. Search this for 'self host potpie', 'firebase_service_account.json', 'PORTKEY_API_KEY', 'localhost:8001 login 401'.

documents.name: Potpie Docs — Agents Introduction
documents.title: Introduction to Potpie Agents
documents.summary: Overview of the five specialized prebuilt agents: Codebase Q&A, Unit Test, Integration Test, Debugging, and Code Changes.
documents.description: The hub page for Potpie's suite of specialized prebuilt agents, each leveraging the code knowledge graph and code-analysis tools. It indexes five agents: the Codebase Q&A Agent (answers questions about functionality, architecture and structure, with `@function` entry-point references), the Unit Test Agent (test plans and unit test code for a given function or class), the Integration Test Agent (test plans from an entry-point function, best on Python/JavaScript/TypeScript), the Debugging with Knowledge Graph Agent (analyzes stacktraces and errors against your codebase, adds print debugging, iterates toward root cause), and the Code Changes Agent (analyzes the current branch against the default branch, identifies impacted APIs and cascading effects). Search this for 'which agent should I use', 'stacktrace agent', 'generate unit tests for my repo', 'which APIs does my change break'.

documents.name: Potpie Docs — Slack Integration
documents.title: PotpieAI Integration for Slack
documents.summary: How to install and authenticate the PotpieAI Slack app so a team can chat with a parsed codebase from Slack.
documents.description: The user-facing guide for the Slack extension. Prerequisites are a PotpieAI account with an API token, at least one project already parsed and in `ready` status, and the PotpieAI Slack app installed in the workspace via the install link on the potpie-slack Cloud Run host. It then covers granting permissions, finding PotpieAI in the workspace apps list, and authenticating the Slack user against a Potpie API token so codebase questions asked in Slack route to the right project. Search this for 'slack bot not responding', 'project not ready status slack', 'potpie slack install link', 'authenticate slack app with API key'.

documents.name: SKILL: potpie-cli
documents.title: Potpie CLI
documents.summary: Bundle skill (version 2) teaching a harness the `potpie` command itself: doctor, login, pot management, source registration, scope behavior.
documents.description: The one bundled skill that is about the tool rather than a use case, and the one skill the Claude Code plugin deliberately does NOT ship (8 in the agent bundle, 7 in the plugin). It tells the harness to prefer a use-case skill for ordinary project-memory context and to reach for this one only when the user is asking about the `potpie` command: `potpie doctor` / `potpie --json doctor`, `make cli-status`, `uv tool list`, `which -a potpie`, `potpie login <api-key> --url <host>`, `potpie pot list|use|info|linked|default set`, and `potpie source add repo .`. Search this for 'potpie command not found', 'which pot am I in', 'register this repo as a source', 'doctor says not configured'.

documents.name: SKILL: potpie-graph
documents.title: Potpie Graph Workbench
documents.summary: The flagship bundle skill (version 5): discover the contract, read named views, resolve identity, propose/commit --verify, inspect quality, use the inbox.
documents.description: The primary read/write skill for the graph workbench, and the one that states the product philosophy most bluntly: 'The graph is project memory... You are the intelligence that reads it before acting and writes durable learnings after. Potpie validates, lowers, commits, audits, and ranks. It does not scan a repository or infer rich facts from prose for you.' It teaches the orientation step first (`potpie graph status`, `potpie graph catalog --task "<task>" --profile read`) which returns contract + ontology versions, readable views and the active match_mode (vector vs lexical), and instructs the agent to trust the live catalog's operation partition over any example in a skill file. It then covers `graph search-entities` for identity resolution, `graph propose` → `graph commit --verify`, `graph quality`, `graph inbox` for parking uncertain work, writing retrieval-grade descriptions, and responding to nudges — preferring the CLI over the MCP context_* tools whenever a shell is available.

documents.name: SKILL: potpie-repo-baseline
documents.title: Potpie Repo Baseline
documents.summary: Bundle skill for establishing or refreshing a repository's baseline memory: purpose, features, services, environments, deps, contracts, ownership, preferences.
documents.description: The harness-led replacement for a repo scanner. It prescribes a fixed procedure: resolve the pot and source (`potpie --json pot info`, `potpie --json source list`, `potpie source add repo . --pot <pot>`) while warning that source registration records metadata only and does not ingest or scan; then discover the live contract (`graph status`, `graph catalog --task "deep repo baseline"`, `graph describe features|infra_topology|decisions --examples`); then read authored and code-adjacent sources and write graph workbench mutations. It is the skill that makes 'ingest this repo' a reasoning task the user's own model performs rather than a deterministic tree walk. Search this for 'baseline a new repo', 'what does this repo do', 'first-time ingestion', 'source add does nothing'.

documents.name: SKILL: potpie-source-ingestion
documents.title: Potpie Source Ingestion
documents.summary: Bundle skill for explicit ingestion of a repo, PR, issue, ticket, runbook, incident report, document or link — todo-driven, evidence-backed.
documents.description: The skill for explicit ingestion requests, built around a set of non-negotiables: use a todo/checklist for every repository or multi-source ingestion and never jump straight from a README to graph writes; local inspection is required and scanner-driven graph updates are forbidden (inspect with `rg`, `rg --files`, `git` and structured tooling, never legacy deterministic ingestion commands that walk the tree and write facts); use subagents only for read-only discovery slices while the main agent owns source selection, identity resolution, mutation proposals, commits and final synthesis; do not write until every required discovery lane is complete, explicitly unavailable, or scoped out; and every write must carry source refs, source authority, truth class, confidence, a compact summary and a retrieval-grade description. It runs phase 0 scope-and-preflight through discovery lanes to propose/verified commit.

documents.name: SKILL: potpie-project-preferences
documents.title: Potpie Project Preferences
documents.summary: Bundle skill loaded before writing or reviewing code so repo conventions surface instead of being rediscovered.
documents.description: Teaches the harness to read project conventions before implementation or review, and to record durable ones afterward. The prescribed fast path is: identify the narrowest scope known (repo, path, service, package, file), expand the user's task into preference search terms (error handling, retries, validation, logging, observability, framework, folder layout, tests, dependency choice, security, API shape, naming), then `potpie graph read --subgraph decisions --view preferences_for_scope --scope repo:<owner-repo>,path:<path-or-dir> --query "<expanded preference query>"`. If the scope is unclear it falls back to `potpie --json pot info` / `source list` or entity search. Search this for 'what conventions does this repo use', 'error handling style here', 'should I use X library', 'record this as a preference'.

documents.name: SKILL: potpie-infra-architecture
documents.title: Potpie Infra Architecture
documents.summary: Bundle skill for environments, adapters, runtime config, service dependencies, datastores, API contracts, ownership and dependency blast radius.
documents.description: The infra-context skill. It tells the agent to start from whichever service, environment, adapter or dependency the task names, resolve identity before assuming keys (`potpie graph search-entities "<service env adapter dependency>" --limit 10`), then read the service neighborhood via `potpie graph read --subgraph infra_topology --view service_neighborhood --scope service:<name> --environment <dev|staging|prod|preview> --depth 2 --direction both`. It is the skill an agent loads when asked 'what will break if I change this dependency', 'which environment does this run in', 'who owns this service', 'what datastores does it touch', or 'what does the blast radius of this config change look like'.

documents.name: SKILL: potpie-change-timeline
documents.title: Potpie Change Timeline
documents.summary: Bundle skill for 'what changed recently': merged PRs, tickets, docs, incidents, deployments, releases, and regression hunting.
documents.description: The timeline skill. Its fast path reads the project timeline first with `potpie graph read --subgraph recent_changes --view timeline --format table --time-window 7d --limit 20`, and it carries an important scoping rule: a pot is the project boundary and can contain multiple repos, so do not narrow to the current repo unless the user asks. It instructs the agent to use the user's exact dates when provided, and covers ingesting source history from GitHub, Linear, Jira, docs and deployment records. This is the skill behind questions like 'what changed last week', 'when did this regress', 'which PR touched this file', 'what shipped before the incident'.

documents.name: SKILL: potpie-debug-memory
documents.title: Potpie Debug Memory
documents.summary: Bundle skill loaded before debugging so prior symptoms, known fixes and failed attempts guide the investigation.
documents.description: The debugging-memory skill, and the one that most depends on retrieval-grade descriptions. Its core instruction is to search by symptom first, not just component name — include exact error text, commands, failing tests, environment, service, dependency and synonyms — via `potpie graph read --subgraph debugging --view prior_occurrences --query "<expanded symptom query>" --scope service:<service-name> --limit 12`, omitting --scope when no service is known. If the failure smells like a regression it tells the agent to correlate with the recent_changes timeline. It covers flaky tests, incidents, production alerts, CI failures, local dev setup issues, repeated bugs, prior fixes, failed attempts and verification history.

documents.name: SKILL: graph-mutation-plan (server-side reconciliation)
documents.title: Composing an apply_graph_mutations plan
documents.summary: Server-side reconciliation cookbook for apply_graph_mutations plans — stable entity_key patterns, label/edge vocabulary, evidence discipline. Stale vs the shipped ontology.
documents.description: One of the two server-side reconciliation skills (version 1.0.0), never installed into a harness and not managed by DefaultSkillManager; it is loaded by `adapters/outbound/reconciliation/pydantic_deep_agent.py` through its own list_skills/load_skill toolset, and the deep agent writes via a different tool surface (apply_graph_mutations, mark_event_processed, finish_batch). It documents plan fields, the stable entity_key cookbook (`github:repo:<owner>/<repo>`, `github:pr:<owner>/<repo>:<n>`, `github:issue:...`, `module:<repo>:<dotted.path>`, `feature:<repo>:<slug>`, `ticket:<source>:<identifier>`, `timeline:activity:<verb>:<short_hex>`, `timeline:period:daily:<pot_id>:<YYYY-MM-DD>`) and the automatic downgrade behavior (entities → Document/Observation, edges → RELATED_TO). It is measurably stale against the shipped 2026-06-graph ontology: its label list still names Incident, DiagnosticSignal and Module, and its plan schema still documents an `episodes` field. Treat its examples as historical, not authoritative.

documents.name: SKILL: backfill-enumerate-drain (server-side reconciliation)
documents.title: Backfill: enumerate, then drain
documents.summary: Server-side reconciliation skill for handling a *.added seed event: enumerate once per list tool, write one todo per ref, drain newest-first, resume without re-enumerating.
documents.description: The second server-side reconciliation skill, loaded when a `*.added` seed event arrives (a repository or team was just connected) with the planner enabled. Its loop is: call each enumerator tool exactly once — they are bounded server-side to a trailing window and a hard item cap and return newest-first, and paging or scraping beyond one call is forbidden because the tail arrives via live webhooks and future backfill; write one todo per returned ref; drain newest-first, hydrating each ref with the detail tool (e.g. github_get_pull_request, github_get_issue) and applying the per-kind extraction via apply_graph_mutations. Its critical resume rule is that the todo list rides in message history checkpointed after every tool call, so a resumed run continues an existing list and must never re-enumerate. The single-event contract requires passing the seed's event_id to every apply_graph_mutations call, then one mark_event_processed followed by finish_batch.

documents.name: potpie README
documents.title: Potpie — Context Graph for AI Native SDLC
documents.summary: The public front door for the 5.5k-star OSS repo: what Potpie is, and the two-step `uv tool install potpie` + `potpie setup` install.
documents.description: The repo-root README for potpie-ai/potpie, the Apache-2.0 public Python repo. Its one-line thesis — 'Potpie turns your codebase and software development lifecycle into a living context graph for AI agents' — is the sentence the vision doc quotes back, and it claims Potpie indexes code, structure, decisions, source history, team knowledge and engineering workflows so agents can answer questions, plan changes, debug failures and write code with project-specific context. Install is two steps: `uv tool install potpie` (recommended over pip because global mutation of Python packages is discouraged), then `potpie setup`, whose wizard provisions local config, storage, the daemon, a default pot and agent skills, and lets the user pick integrations and their coding harness. Badges point at docs.potpie.ai, the test.yml GitHub Actions workflow, the PyPI `potpie` package, and the Discord.

documents.name: potpie-ui AGENTS.md
documents.title: Context Engine (AGENTS.md)
documents.summary: Agent instructions checked into potpie-ui telling harnesses to orient with the four MCP context_* tools and record durable learnings afterward.
documents.description: The repo-root agent-instruction file for potpie-ai/potpie-ui. It tells any harness working in the frontend repo to use the Potpie context engine for project memory before non-trivial work and to record durable learnings after, and it insists on the minimal port: only context_resolve (the primary context wrap, taking intent/scope/include/mode/source_policy/budget), context_status (cheap pot readiness and freshness gaps), context_search (narrow follow-up after resolve) and context_record (save decisions, fixes, preferences, workflows, bug patterns, feature notes, incident summaries, doc references), with an explicit rule not to add separate tools per context type. It then lists JSON 'recipes' for feature work, debugging, review, operations, docs and onboarding. Parts of it have drifted: the quick-start block still shows the retired `potpie search` / `potpie ingest` / `potpie pot pots` commands, and its debugging recipe requests include names like `diagnostic_signals`, `incidents` and `alerts` that the shipped include vocabulary no longer exposes.

documents.name: potpie-workflows SECURITY.md
documents.title: Security Guidelines
documents.summary: Dependency-security guidance for the private workflows repo, anchored on the Werkzeug debugger CVE and a hard no-debug-in-production rule.
documents.description: The security policy checked into potpie-ai/potpie-workflows, written as a living record of remediations rather than a disclosure policy. Its worked example is CVE-2024-34069, the Werkzeug debugger vulnerability where an attacker controlling a domain and subdomain can execute code on a developer's machine by tricking them into entering the debugger PIN; the mitigation is a `werkzeug>=3.0.3` constraint in pyproject.toml even though the service runs FastAPI + Uvicorn and never uses the Werkzeug debugger, so a transitive dependency cannot reintroduce a vulnerable version. It then states the critical operational rule that debug mode must never be enabled in production, and notes the repo uses `debugpy` (configured in .vscode/launch.json) plus `uvicorn --reload` for local development only. It is the human-readable counterpart to the long stream of Vanta/Dependabot CVE-remediation PRs that dominate this repo's history.

documents.name: potpie-workflows Recipe API Contract
documents.title: Recipe API Contract
documents.summary: Endpoint-by-endpoint contract for the recipe/question-generation API on :8002 — statuses, payloads, and the question → spec → plan task chain.
documents.description: The API contract the potpie-ui build flow is written against, despite the filename still saying QUESTION_GENERATION_API. It documents the base URL `http://localhost:8002/api/v1/recipes`, Bearer-token auth on every endpoint, and each operation starting with `GET /api/v1/recipes/` for the authenticated user's recipes. The recipe object it returns is the shape the frontend renders: id, project_id, user_prompt, additional_links, status (e.g. PENDING_QUESTIONS), created_by, the three task-id slots current_question_task_id / current_spec_task_id / current_plan_task_id, the generated specification and plan, plus repo_name, branch_name and created_at. Search this for 'recipe status PENDING_QUESTIONS', 'spec generate stream endpoint', 'answers payload shape', 'why is current_plan_task_id null'.

documents.name: Context Engine & Copilot Onboarding Platform — Delivery Roadmap v1
documents.title: Context Engine & Copilot Onboarding Platform — Delivery Roadmap (v1 DRAFT)
documents.summary: The enterprise pilot plan: 6 two-week sprints delivering a context engine + Copilot onboarding agents for Siemens X-ray config management.
documents.description: The customer-facing delivery roadmap that defines what the private `pie` (Enterprise potpie) repo is for. It scopes a 12-week, six-sprint pilot for Siemens X-ray Systems, targeting new-hire onboarding in the Configuration Management & Updates subsystem, with Copilot as the user-facing surface and software engineers as the target users. The sprint arc runs from access and infrastructure enablement (VPN, firewall, repo/wiki/ALM access, LLM provider approval, Copilot licenses and extensibility permissions), through context-engine and store-layer deployment, into context collection, graph construction and evaluation design, then intensive graph tuning alongside Copilot integration, and finally pilot validation and handover. Its success criteria are agreed in Sprint 4 rather than after delivery: the primary lagging metric is mean time to first commit / first merged PR for new engineers, with retrieval-quality scores against a signed-off evaluation question set and pilot adoption as leading indicators, and a go-live gate on the Sprint-4 quality bar.

documents.name: RFC: splitting potpie into product, engine and core
documents.title: RFC — the product / context-engine / context-core package split
documents.summary: Internal RFC (POT-1897) proposing the three-way split of the potpie monorepo into the product app, the context-engine, and a dependency-light context-core.
documents.description: An internal RFC arguing that the single `potpie` package had become three products wearing one setup.py: the hosted product app (parsing, agents, conversations, sandbox), the context-engine (CLI, daemon, graph workbench, ontology, readers), and a dependency-light core carrying the ontology, contract constants and DTOs. Its motivating pain is concrete — installing the CLI from PyPI dragged in torch and sentence-transformers via the product's optional embedder path, and the import-time ontology coherence guards were being imported by consumers that only needed the vocabulary. It proposes `potpie/context-core/` as the shared vocabulary package with zero heavy dependencies, `potpie/context-engine/` depending on it, and the legacy product app under `legacy/` shrinking over time. Rejected alternatives: publishing three separate GitHub repos (too much cross-repo version churn for a team this size), and keeping one package with extras (does not fix the coherence-guard import cost). Filed under Linear POT-1897.

documents.name: Runbook: draining the ingestion event backlog
documents.title: On-call runbook — ingestion backlog and stuck reconciliation batches
documents.summary: Internal on-call procedure for when the Postgres ingestion event store backs up or events wedge in `processing`.
documents.description: The runbook the on-call reaches for when the internal Postgres event store backs up — symptoms being a growing `queued` count on `/api/v1/context/pots/{pot_id}/events`, events stuck in `processing` past their lease, or the pot events console in potpie-ui showing an ingestion pipeline that never advances. It walks the triage order: confirm which composition root is affected (the HTTP ingestion server on neo4j, not the local falkordb_lite daemon), check the four lifecycle states `queued / processing / done / error` rather than the retired six-state vocabulary, identify whether the stall is webhook intake or the celery context-graph worker, and only then retry individual events via `POST /api/v1/context/events/{event_id}/retry`. It includes the guardrail that a mass-retry can duplicate work only if entity keys are unstable, which is why the stable-key cookbook is a correctness dependency of this runbook, and the escalation path to the core context-graph team.

documents.name: Graph quality review — June 2026
documents.title: Graph quality review, June 2026 cycle
documents.summary: Monthly review of `graph quality` output across demo and internal pots: duplicate candidates, stale facts, orphan entities and thin descriptions.
documents.description: The recurring internal review that reads `potpie graph quality summary|duplicate-candidates|stale-facts|conflicting-claims|orphan-entities` across the internal pots and turns the output into work. The June 2026 cycle's headline findings were: a long tail of orphan entities minted as edge endpoints and then never referenced again; duplicate candidates concentrated on Person and Service keys where one agent used a display name and another used a handle; and a large fraction of claims carrying descriptions under the retrieval-card bar, which the ontology treats as a warning rather than a reject and which therefore silently degrades recall in `prior_occurrences` and `preferences_for_scope` reads. It also tallies QualityIssue markers by downgrade kind, which is how the label-downgrade and RELATED_TO-fallback counts in this graph are tracked over time. Search this for 'why is retrieval bad', 'duplicate entity keys', 'thin descriptions', 'orphan entity cleanup'.

documents.name: Playbook: Vanta / Dependabot CVE remediation
documents.title: Dependency vulnerability remediation playbook
documents.summary: Internal playbook for the recurring Vanta and Dependabot vulnerability sweeps across all eight potpie repos.
documents.description: The internal procedure behind the steady stream of 'fixed high/med/critical vanta vulnerabilities' PRs that dominate potpie-workflows, pie and potpie-ui history. It defines the severity-to-SLA mapping, the order of operations (bump the direct constraint in pyproject.toml or package.json, regenerate uv.lock / pnpm-lock.yaml, re-run the test suite, never pin a transitive dependency in a lockfile alone), and the rule that a constraint added purely to block a transitive downgrade must be documented in the repo's SECURITY.md so the next engineer does not remove it as unused. It names the repeat offenders seen in practice — joserfc, h11/uvicorn, python-multipart, form-data, dompurify, js-yaml, protobufjs, websocket-driver and pyo3 in the Rust parsing extension — and assigns the sweep to the infra-security rotation. Tracked under Linear POT-1742.

documents.name: Context graph repair roadmap (2026-07-08)
documents.title: Context-graph repair roadmap
documents.summary: Working roadmap of the 🔧 tools the agent-mutation-flow doc depends on: graph map, graph resolve, entity cards, propose annotations, identity delta, reconcile phase.
documents.description: The scratch roadmap that agent-mutation-flow.md cites by path as the source of its 🔧 markers. It enumerates the missing pieces between the shipped write path and the ideal agent loop: a `graph map` orientation command that summarises what a pot already contains and its naming habits; `graph resolve` / `graph entities` / entity cards so an agent can match candidates against existing keys instead of guessing; against-store annotations on `graph propose` so the check stage can say 'this key already exists with a different label'; an identity delta on `graph commit --verify`; and a first-class reconcile phase wrapping `graph quality` plus `graph inbox`. Its framing argument is that the 2026-07-02 end-to-end run proved prose discipline in a SKILL.md does not survive contact with real agents, so each hand-off must become a checkable typed artifact. Tracked under Linear POT-1955; lives in .tmp/ and is not published with the doc set.

observations.name: potpie-workflows PR traffic is dominated by CVE remediation, not features
observations.summary: Roughly two thirds of recent potpie-workflows PRs are Vanta/Dependabot vulnerability sweeps rather than product work.
observations.description: Reading the potpie-workflows pull-request history, the dominant signal is dependency security, not feature delivery: of the last ~40 PRs, the large majority are titled some variant of 'fixed high/med/critical vanta vulnerabilities', '[Vanta] Fix High vulnerabilities in potpie-workflows', 'fix: patch CVE-2025-43859 — update h11 and uvicorn', 'fix: upgrade joserfc to remediate CVE-2026-48990' or 'chore(deps): bump python-multipart'. The actual product PRs are a thin band — specgen replaced with a two-phase deep agent, multi-batch structured Q&A, the plangen redesign, codegen changes — and they cluster around a handful of authors while the CVE stream is spread across shmbhvi101, Harigithub11, kshitij2040 and the cursor GitHub app. The practical consequence for anyone querying this repo's timeline: a naive 'what changed recently' read returns almost entirely dependency bumps and will mislead an agent about where the engineering effort actually went.

observations.name: The potpie CLI issue cluster is dominated by timezone and intent-detection defects
observations.summary: Open CLI/MCP bug reports repeatedly land on naive-datetime crashes in recency scoring and on flags that are accepted but never affect retrieval.
observations.description: The bug reports filed against the potpie CLI and MCP surface form a tight cluster with two recurring shapes. The first is datetime handling in the read trunk: '[Bug] MCP: date-only or naive as_of crashes context_resolve/context_search with TypeError in recency scoring' — a naive datetime reaching the ranker's recency factor and blowing up on comparison with an aware timestamp. The second, larger shape is flags that are accepted and documented but silently inert: 'CLI: resolve --mode is accepted, documented, and recommended but never affects retrieval', 'CLI: resolve defaults to feature intent without detection', 'Graph read CLI flags accepted but ignored on default read path', 'CLI skill advertises unsupported search flags', and 'graph read succeeds when required scope is missing'. Together they describe a surface whose contract is wider than its implementation, which is why the querying doc's anti-phantom-vocabulary rule (return `unknown_include`, never a silent zero) exists. Reporters are concentrated in AdityaPainuli, Nih1tGupta and Dsantra92.

observations.name: potpie-ui PR authorship is split between humans and GitHub apps
observations.summary: A meaningful share of potpie-ui and potpie-workflows PRs are authored by the cursor and potpie-agent GitHub apps rather than by a person.
observations.description: Sampling recent pull requests across the frontend and workflows repos, author attribution is not purely human: alongside shmbhvi101, BrhKmr23, ASCE-D, yashkrishan, nndn and LaibaFirdouse, a recurring block of PRs is opened by `app/cursor` (Vanta vulnerability sweeps) and `app/potpie-agent` (e.g. 'Add architecture documentation'), plus `app/dependabot` for routine bumps. This matters for any ownership or contribution question asked of this graph: PERFORMED/AUTHORED edges attributed to a bot app say something about tooling adoption, not about who understands the change, and 'who should I ask about this' answers must fall back to reviewers or to the surrounding human commits. It is also a live example of the agent-authored-change loop Potpie is built to record — the org is dogfooding agent-opened PRs on its own repos.

observations.name: Two competing evidence-strength vocabularies exist in the ontology code
observations.summary: ontology.EVIDENCE_STRENGTHS and the ranker's _STRENGTH_TO_SCORE disagree; only the ranker's set is consumed.
observations.description: The ontology documentation carries an explicit caveat that two evidence-strength vocabularies coexist in `domain/`. `ontology.EVIDENCE_STRENGTHS` is the older tuple (deterministic, attested, inferred, hypothesized) with DEFAULT_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH='inferred', while `domain/ranking.py _STRENGTH_TO_SCORE` uses (deterministic, attested, stated, inferred, speculative) scoring 1.0 down to 0.2. The TRUTH_TO_EVIDENCE_STRENGTH map that turns a claim's truth class into rank weight targets the ranker vocabulary, so the older set has `hypothesized` which nothing scores and lacks `stated` and `speculative` which everything scores. Anyone writing a claim by hand, reading a `breakdown.strength` value, or debugging 'why did this claim rank low' needs to know which of the two they are looking at. It is a live drift the import-time coherence guards do not currently catch because the two sets live in different modules with different consumers.

observations.name: The graph-mutation-plan SKILL.md is stale relative to the shipped schema
observations.summary: The server-side reconciliation skill still names Incident/DiagnosticSignal/Module labels and an `episodes` plan field that the shipped ontology and Pydantic schema do not have.
observations.description: The server-side reconciliation cookbook at adapters/outbound/reconciliation/skills/graph-mutation-plan/SKILL.md is version 1.0.0 and predates the 2026-06-graph ontology. Its canonical-vocabulary section still lists `Incident`, `DiagnosticSignal` and `Module` as entity labels — none of which exist in the 24-label catalog, where incidents collapse into Activity with activity_type='incident', diagnostic signals become Observation or BugPattern, and modules become CodeAsset. Its stable-key cookbook still teaches `module:<repo>:<dotted.path>`, and its plan-fields section documents an `episodes` array ({name, episode_body, source_description, reference_time}) that the shipped mutation schema no longer accepts, a leftover of the removed Graphiti episodic ingestion path. Because the soft-fail validator downgrades rather than rejects, a deep-agent run following this skill produces silently degraded output — Incident nodes landing as Document/Observation and unknown edges landing as RELATED_TO at confidence 0.3 — instead of a loud failure. The skill's own instruction to trust the live catalog over any skill example is the mitigation.

observations.name: Context-graph docs carry commit-pinned status headers, and one has drifted ahead
observations.summary: Every context-graph doc states the commit it reflects; eleven say 8dd175bc/2026-06-29 while cli-flow.md says 49e12528/2026-07-02.
observations.description: The context-graph doc set uses a discipline worth noting: each file opens with a status line naming the commit it reflects and the date it was last reviewed. Eleven of them read 'reflects code on main @ 8dd175bc, last reviewed 2026-06-29'; cli-flow.md reads '@ 49e12528, last reviewed 2026-07-02'; agent-mutation-flow.md instead declares itself a design target drafted 2026-07-09 and warns not to treat it as current-state reference. The convention makes doc staleness measurable rather than a guess, and it is the reason a reader can trust the ontology and writing docs over any SKILL.md example. The flip side is that a single doc drifting ahead of the pinned commit (as cli-flow.md has) is the earliest signal that the rest of the set is due for a review pass.

observations.name: The word 'ledger' means two unrelated things in this codebase
observations.summary: The live internal Postgres event store and the mostly-stubbed external Event Ledger product share a name and are routinely confused.
observations.description: A persistent source of confusion documented at the top of ingestion-nudge.md: 'ledger' refers both to the REAL internal Postgres event store (adapters/outbound/postgres/{reconciliation_ledger,ingestion_event_store,batch_repository,ledger}.py), which is a live work queue with lifecycle states queued/processing/done/error and no cursor concept, and to the external Event Ledger product seam (domain/ports/ledger/*, adapters/outbound/ledger/{managed,self_hosted}_client.py), which owns provider credentials, webhooks, normalized source history and a per-(pot, source) cursor — and which is mostly TODO stubs, so `ledger pull/query/status` is non-functional against any real provider. The older six-state vocabulary (pending/processing/applied/failed_retryable/failed_terminal/timed_out) described the external consumer that does not exist yet, so any monitoring, runbook or dashboard built on those six states is describing a system that was never shipped.

observations.name: Managed-backend routing is designed but raises CapabilityNotImplemented
observations.summary: `pot use --managed`, `pot list --managed` and the whole `cloud` command group are documented roadmap surfaces that are not functional.
observations.description: Three separate docs (context-graph README, bench-plan, ingestion-nudge) carry the same roadmap warning: the managed-backend profile is designed, documented and reachable from the CLI surface, but every managed path raises CapabilityNotImplemented. That covers `potpie pot use --managed`, `potpie pot list --managed` and the entire `cloud` command group, plus the managed backend profile as a benchmark target. State stays local by default and the shipped default backend is the embedded falkordb_lite. The signal for agents and for anyone triaging a support question: a CapabilityNotImplemented traceback from a `--managed` or `cloud` command is expected behavior, not a broken install, and the correct answer is to stay on the local profile rather than to debug credentials.

observations.name: potpie-ui AGENTS.md recipes reference retired commands and include names
observations.summary: The checked-in agent instructions still show `potpie search` / `potpie ingest` / `potpie pot pots` and includes like diagnostic_signals and incidents.
observations.description: The AGENTS.md at the root of potpie-ui is the file every harness working in the frontend repo loads first, and parts of it have drifted from the shipped CLI. Its quick-start block advertises `potpie search "topic"`, `potpie ingest "..."` and `potpie pot pots`, none of which match the current command surface documented in cli-flow.md, and its debugging recipe requests include names — `diagnostic_signals`, `incidents`, `alerts`, `deployments` — that the shipped include vocabulary in domain/agent_context_port.py does not expose. Because the read trunk implements an anti-phantom-vocabulary rule, those includes come back as `unknown_include` rather than silently empty, which makes the drift visible but still wastes a round trip on every task started in this repo. This is the frontend-repo instance of the same staleness pattern seen in the server-side reconciliation skill.

observations.name: The two composition roots default to different graph backends
observations.summary: host_wiring.py defaults to embedded falkordb_lite while bootstrap/ingestion_server.py defaults to neo4j — the most common architectural confusion in this codebase.
observations.description: Architecture.md names conflating the two composition roots as the single most common mistake, and the concrete tell is the default backend. The local agent spine (`potpie/services/host_wiring.py`, driving the CLI, daemon and MCP tools) defaults to `falkordb_lite`, an embedded FalkorDB over a local file requiring no Docker, server or cloud key. The HTTP ingestion server (`bootstrap/ingestion_server.py`, which owns webhook intake, the Postgres event store and the off-by-default reconciliation deep agent) defaults to `neo4j`. The local OSS CLI/daemon path never runs the ingestion server, and local repo baseline is harness-led via skills instead. Symptoms of the confusion in practice: 'my webhook events never show up in `graph read`', 'why does the CLI not need Neo4j', and 'ingestion works in prod but not locally' — all three are the same misunderstanding.

observations.name: Two parallel repo-materialization stacks are still live in potpie
observations.summary: The hexagonal app/src/sandbox module and the legacy repo_manager + code_changes_manager stack both run; the integration plan to retire the old one is unfinished.
observations.description: The sandbox integration plan documents a duplication that has not yet been resolved: `app/src/sandbox/sandbox/` is hexagonal, runnable, idempotent and E2E-tested across subprocess, docker and daytona runtimes, while the rest of potpie still drives `app/modules/repo_manager/` (bare repo + worktree management under .repos/<owner>/<repo>/ with its own auth chain, eviction and metadata) and `app/modules/intelligence/tools/code_changes_manager/` (a Redis-backed per-conversation file-edit staging area wrapped in roughly twenty LangChain StructuredTools including git_commit, git_push and bash_command). Parsing still calls RepoManager.prepare_for_parsing() and walks the worktree with os.walk plus Tree-sitter. The practical hazard is two eviction policies and two clone paths for the same repo on the same disk, which is the shape of bug to suspect when a repo appears cached but an agent cannot see recent files.

observations.name: Security remediation is concentrated on one contributor across every repo
observations.summary: shmbhvi101 authors dependency and CVE fixes in potpie, potpie-ui, potpie-workflows, pie and the slack bot — a single point of coverage.
observations.description: Tracing dependency-remediation authorship across the org shows the same handle appearing in every repository: shmbhvi101 files the vulnerability sweeps in potpie-workflows ('fix: remediate high-risk Python dependency vulnerabilities', 'fix: upgrade joserfc to remediate CVE-2026-48990'), the frontend package bumps in potpie-ui, and CLI-facing fixes in potpie ('fix(cli): surface uv-tool install facts in doctor and docs', 'fix(cli): explain missing service logs for embedded graph backends'). The Vanta compliance cadence that drives this work is org-wide and recurring rather than incidental. The graph-level observation worth surfacing to a reader: security knowledge here is concentrated rather than distributed, so a 'who owns dependency security for repo X' query resolves to the same person regardless of X, and bus-factor risk on the remediation playbook is real.

observations.name: The k8s deployment repo still uses pre-rename 'momentum' service names
observations.summary: potpie-k8s-deployments manifests and Jenkinsfiles refer to momentum-core, momentum-server, mom-api and knowledge-graph rather than current service names.
observations.description: The infrastructure repo predates the product rename and never fully caught up. Its prod README describes the deployed microservices as knowledge-graph, momentum-core, momentum-server and 'momentum as micro-services: celery, mom-api, conversation-api (mom-api)', with directory names like `prod/mom-server-microsvc/{celery,convo,mom-api}` alongside neo4j-cluster, PgBouncer, vault, cert-manager and the ingress controller, all driven by Jenkinsfiles rather than GitOps. This means any topology question answered from code (service names in potpie) and any question answered from deployment manifests (service names in k8s) use different vocabularies for the same workloads, and a reader searching for 'mom-api' will find infra but no application code, while a reader searching for 'convo-server' finds the reverse.

observations.name: The VS Code C/C++ debug fix was smoke-tested, not matrix-tested
observations.summary: The debug handoff verified terminal exec, adapter discovery, session start and breakpoints, but snapshot-after-continue still fails and most DAP verbs were never exercised.
observations.description: The VS Code extension debug handoff is explicit that its verification run was a smoke test rather than a full DAP tool matrix. Verified: /api/terminal/execute returning in ~400ms with success=true and exit_code=0 for `cc -g -o add_numbers add_numbers.c`; /api/workspace/debug-context returning ["python","node","lldb","lldb-dap"] after the adapter-discovery fix; /api/debug/start-session with lldb-dap returning a session id; /api/debug/set-breakpoints returning a verified breakpoint at add_numbers.c:4. Still failing: /api/debug/snapshot after continue, with 'Cannot take snapshot: session is running, expected paused'. Never exercised: step-over, step-into, step-out, evaluate, list-sessions and a clean stop-session path. Anyone treating C/C++ debugging as fixed should read the unverified list first — the residual RPC-timeout failure mode (tool_call emitted, no tool_response on Redis pub/sub before timeout) is the one most likely to resurface.

observations.name: The public docs site still carries Mintlify starter-kit boilerplate
observations.summary: mintlify-docs keeps the template README, the sample plant-store API reference and the essentials/* pages alongside real Potpie content.
observations.description: The potpie-ai/mintlify-docs repo was bootstrapped from the Mintlify starter kit and never fully cleaned. Its repo README is still the template's 'Click on Use this template to copy the Mintlify starter kit', api-reference/introduction.mdx still contains the starter Note saying the section can be deleted if you are not building API reference docs and still links the Plant Store OpenAPI sample, and the whole essentials/ tree (settings, markdown, code, navigation, images, reusable-snippets) plus snippets/snippet-intro.mdx is unmodified template content. The genuine Potpie pages are introduction, quickstart, self-hosting/*, custom-agents/*, agents/* and extensions/slack. For retrieval this matters: a semantic search over the docs repo will surface template prose that describes Mintlify rather than Potpie unless the essentials and api-reference sample pages are excluded.

quality_issues.name: Component label downgraded to CodeAsset
quality_issues.summary: A reconciliation plan emitted entity label `Component`, which is not in the 24-label catalog; soft-fail rewrote it to CodeAsset.
quality_issues.description: A server-side reconciliation batch minted entities labelled `Component` for subsystem-shaped concepts (parsing, conversations, the graph workbench). `Component` was removed from the ontology when the 2026-06-graph catalog collapsed subsystem labels onto CodeAsset (a file/module/package anchor) or Service (if independently runnable). With CONTEXT_ENGINE_ONTOLOGY_SOFT_FAIL=1 the pre-apply gate in application/services/reconciliation_validation.py dropped the unknown label and re-anchored the entities as CodeAsset rather than failing the batch, attaching this QualityIssue marker per downgrade. Symptom for a reader: a code-anchor entity whose description talks about a 'component' and whose key does not resolve to a real path. Fix direction is to re-author the mutation against `graph catalog` output instead of a skill example.

quality_issues.name: Incident label downgraded — incidents must be Activity
quality_issues.summary: A plan following the stale graph-mutation-plan skill emitted `Incident` entities; there is no Incident label, so they fell to Document/Observation.
quality_issues.description: The server-side graph-mutation-plan SKILL.md still lists `Incident` in its canonical entity vocabulary, so a deep-agent reconciliation run minted Incident nodes for production events. The shipped ontology has no Incident label: Activity is the single timeline collapse point and an incident is an Activity with activity_type='incident' and a verb_class such as 'incident_resolved'. Soft-fail downgrade turned the unknown label into Document/Observation, which means those events dropped out of every timeline read (`--subgraph recent_changes --view timeline`) because the reader filters on is_activity. This is the highest-impact of the stale-skill downgrades: the facts survive but become unreachable from the query that needs them.

quality_issues.name: Module label and module: key pattern downgraded to CodeAsset
quality_issues.summary: Entities keyed `module:<repo>:<dotted.path>` per the stale skill cookbook were downgraded to CodeAsset with non-canonical keys.
quality_issues.description: The graph-mutation-plan skill's stable-key cookbook teaches `module:<repo>:<dotted.path>` for modules and packages, but `Module` is not one of the 24 labels and `module:` is not a registered key prefix — CodeAsset owns both, keyed `code:<repo>:<path>`. Plans following the cookbook produced entities that soft-fail relabelled as CodeAsset while keeping a dotted-path key, so they never collide with the path-keyed CodeAssets minted by harness-led baselines of the same repo. The visible symptom is duplicate coverage of the same file under two keys, which then shows up in `graph quality duplicate-candidates`. Remediation is a key rewrite plus supersession of the dotted-path entities, not a delete.

quality_issues.name: DiagnosticSignal label downgraded to Observation
quality_issues.summary: `DiagnosticSignal` entities from the stale reconciliation vocabulary fell to the generic Observation label, losing their debugging-subgraph affinity.
quality_issues.description: `DiagnosticSignal` appears in the graph-mutation-plan skill's label list and in the potpie-ui AGENTS.md debugging recipe's include list, but it exists in neither the 24-label ontology nor the shipped include vocabulary. Signals of this kind belong on BugPattern (with symptom_signature and first_seen) when they are reproducible failure shapes, or on Observation when they are softer signals. The soft-fail gate took the generic route and relabelled them Observation, which is lossy: an Observation carries no symptom_signature, so a `--subgraph debugging --view prior_occurrences` symptom search cannot match on the error string the signal was created to record. This is the mechanism by which stale vocabulary quietly degrades debug recall.

quality_issues.name: DOCUMENTS edge type downgraded to RELATED_TO
quality_issues.summary: Doc-to-subject edges authored as `DOCUMENTS` are not in the 26-predicate catalog and were rewritten to RELATED_TO at confidence 0.3.
quality_issues.description: Older authoring guidance used a `DOCUMENTS` predicate to link a document to the service, repo or feature it describes. The 2026-06-graph catalog removed it — the rename table maps DOCUMENTS onto MENTIONS or AFFECTS, and MENTIONS is restricted to @Activity → * so it cannot originate from a Document. Plans emitting DOCUMENTS therefore hit the unknown-edge-type path in reconciliation_validation.py and were rewritten to RELATED_TO with confidence forced to 0.3, which is well below the rank threshold most reads use. The practical effect is that documents stop surfacing alongside the entities they explain. The correct authoring pattern under this contract is an explicit Document → RELATED_TO → subject edge authored as an agent_claim with a deliberate confidence, which is what this fixture emits.

quality_issues.name: PART_OF and FIXES edge types downgraded to RELATED_TO
quality_issues.summary: Retired predicates from the older demo vocabulary (PART_OF, FIXES, IMPLEMENTS, RESOLVES) were rewritten to RELATED_TO instead of their renamed equivalents.
quality_issues.description: The ontology's rename table is explicit: PART_OF becomes IMPLEMENTED_IN or TOUCHED, DOCUMENTS becomes MENTIONS or AFFECTS, RESOLVES becomes RESOLVED, and IMPLEMENTS becomes IMPLEMENTED_IN. There are also deliberately no temporal or causal edges — no TRIGGERED_BY, PRECEDED_BY, HOTSPOT, CAUSED, CALLS, DELIVERS, WATCHES, INVESTIGATES, PARTICIPATED_IN or DEPLOYS — because the timeline is a read-time query over valid_at. A batch authored against the old vocabulary emitted PART_OF and FIXES edges; soft-fail rewrote every one to RELATED_TO at confidence 0.3 rather than applying the rename map, so the semantic relation was lost even though a correct target predicate existed. Repairing this requires re-authoring, since the downgrade is not reversible from the stored edge.

quality_issues.name: authoritative_fact claims committed without evidence
quality_issues.summary: Topology edges asserted at truth=authoritative_fact carried no source ref, violating EVIDENCE_REQUIRED_TRUTH_CLASSES.
quality_issues.description: The contract defines EVIDENCE_REQUIRED_TRUTH_CLASSES = {authoritative_fact, source_observation}: objective facts must cite a strong authority such as a file path, a PR reference or a ticket id. A batch of service-to-repository and service-to-datastore topology edges was committed at authoritative_fact with an empty evidence field, so the ranker scored them `deterministic` (weight 1.2) on the strength of a claim nobody can check. The write path treats a material plan with no provenance as a non-blocking evidence warning rather than a reject, which is why these landed. Remediation is either to attach the real source ref (code:<path>, github:<owner>/<repo>#<n>, linear:POT-####) or to downgrade the claim to agent_claim with an honest confidence.

quality_issues.name: `episodes` plan field silently dropped — no longer in the mutation schema
quality_issues.summary: Reconciliation plans still populate an `episodes` array documented by the stale skill; the Pydantic mutation schema has no such field, so the narrative text is discarded.
quality_issues.description: The graph-mutation-plan skill documents a plan field `episodes: {name, episode_body, source_description, reference_time?}` for retaining narrative or source text such as a PR body. That field is a leftover of the removed Graphiti episodic-ingestion path (scrubbed in the EpisodicGraphPort cleanup) and does not exist on the shipped Pydantic mutation schema, so a deep agent that follows the skill writes a payload whose episode bodies are dropped at parse time. Nothing fails and nothing warns — the entities and edges in the same plan apply normally — so the loss is invisible unless someone notices that ingested PRs carry no narrative. It is also consistent with the vision doc's claims-not-payloads rule, which says the graph deliberately never stores PR bodies, meaning the field should be deleted from the skill rather than reinstated in the schema.

quality_issues.name: Server-side reconciliation skill names labels that no longer exist
quality_issues.summary: graph-mutation-plan SKILL.md v1.0.0 teaches a pre-2026-06 vocabulary, which is the upstream cause of the Incident/Module/DiagnosticSignal downgrades.
quality_issues.description: This marker records the root cause rather than an individual downgraded entity: the reconciliation skill file itself is stale. Version 1.0.0 of graph-mutation-plan/SKILL.md names Incident, DiagnosticSignal and Module as canonical labels, teaches a `module:` key prefix, and documents an `episodes` plan field — all removed by the 2026-06-graph ontology. Because the deep agent loads skills from `_SKILLS_DIR` at runtime and the soft-fail validator downgrades rather than rejects, every batch this agent authors inherits the drift silently. The skills doc already prescribes the mitigation in prose ('trust the catalog's current operation partition over any example in a skill file'), but nothing enforces it. The durable fix is to generate the skill's vocabulary section from domain/ontology.py so it cannot drift, matching the module rule that adding an entity is one row in the catalog.
